title: A cup of sun on still water

events.text: AI painter: an imagined yellow pond lily and unequal green pads on dark water, inspired by NPS Denali pond lilies. Goal: join loaded broad planes before veins, and keep one compact yellow light.
Four water lanes remain separate. Broad intermediate washes will join them, keeping the outer linen edge.
The water is joined with soft bands. Place the large left pad as filled planes rather than an outline.
The left pad is filled, with regular ridges and a faceted rim. Add a smaller cooler pad behind the future flower.
A water-colored slit remains in the smaller pad. Two diagonal bridges will close it; the flower stem rises between the pads.
The slit is closed. The stem reads as a narrow curve; build a golden cup with broad left, base and right planes.
The cup is filled but wide and faceted. A curved back rim and darker inset will give the opening depth.
The inset now reads as an opening. The pads need characteristic narrow notches, aimed toward their centers.
Notches are blunt blue slits rather than clean wedges. Broad green neighbors can taper their inner tips and connect the light plane.
Upper review: the back rim is clear but the flower face is one gold mass. Warm shadow at right and a broad pale left plane will turn it.
The left face is lighter but broken into patches. Quiet water reflections will anchor the pads before a loaded flower correction.
The watercolor reflection remains softer than the oil pads. Test one compact loaded light on the flower rim.
The 14px glint survives whole view. Support it with a larger quiet plane, then suggest the raised central disk inside the cup.
The center disk separates from its dark surround. Sparse unequal veins can describe the large pad without covering its quiet planes.
Fine veins barely register at whole view and make small hooks close up. Try fewer wider low-contrast veins on the smaller pad.
The wider veins remain quiet too. A small unopened bud at left will vary the upright rhythm without competing with the yellow cup.
The bud is quieter than the flower. Long sampled reed curves at the right can frame the open water; keep their ends tapered.
The reeds taper but retain elbows. Lower reflections can interrupt the horizontal wash bands without adding another hard oil rail.
Lower review: watercolor ripples are soft and nearly vanish; pad edges float without a crisp contact. Add short broken contact accents, not full outlines.
Short oil contacts sharpened the bottoms but made raised rails. A low-body blue cover outside the right pad will test whether color and relief respond differently.
Thin blue covers changed the color but widened raised rails: a failed correction retained as evidence. Return to the flower, separating two broad front sepals with short warm creases.
The flower creases stay subdued under broader paint. The large pad notch still ends as a blunt bar; taper its lower edge with loaded green, preserving a narrow water opening.
Green neighbors narrowed the slits and left raised patch edges. Round the large pad crown with a sampled broad arc and link its light plane.
The crown pass changed color modestly but left diagonal patch edges. Two broad diagonal bridges can absorb their contrast; the smaller pad needs the same plane continuity.
The bridges reduced little contrast; extra pad covers are no longer helping. Keep their ridges and refine the cup crown with a sampled asymmetric arc.
The crown became rounder but the dark opening lost width. Restore two short inner recesses around the disk, keeping the light at left.
The two recesses separate the disk and the glint remains compact. The bud is blunt at its tip; one tapered crest and a curved calyx will distinguish it from a small leaf.
The bud crest remains blunt and the reed bend partly softened. Connect the stem to a broken, soft reflection rather than another hard outline.
The soft reflection is connected and remains subordinate. Final refinement: restore the small rim glint, support its plane, and join the stem into the cup base.

Finished at 112 marks: broad filled pads and a rounded golden cup hold against soft water; one compact rim light stays focal. Retained regular bristles, blunt notches and bud, reed elbows and raised blue contact repairs. Thin blue covers changed color but enlarged relief. Stop because more covers now add texture faster than clarity.
